test.name: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques - Test 2

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A mixture of two liquids (b.p. 80°C and 85°C) shows an \( R_f \) difference of 0.3 in paper chromatography. Which technique is most efficient for large-scale separation?

text_solutions: Close boiling points (5°C difference) require fractional distillation for large-scale separation, as chromatography is better for analytical purposes.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method cannot be used to estimate nitrogen in compounds containing nitro groups?

text_solutions: Kjeldahl’s method fails for nitro compounds (\( \ce{-NO2} \)) as nitrogen is not easily converted to \( \ce{NH3} \); Dumas method is preferred.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a free radical?

text_solutions: A free radical has an unpaired electron. \( \ce{CH3.} \) is formed by homolytic cleavage and has an unpaired electron on carbon.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which functional group is present in \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) (propanal) contains the \( \ce{-CHO} \) group, characteristic of aldehydes.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification method is most suitable for separating a mixture of two liquids with boiling points of 98°C and 102°C, both miscible in water?

text_solutions: Close boiling points (4°C difference) require fractional distillation for effective separation, as simple distillation is insufficient and solubility doesn’t aid here.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound \( \ce{C5H10O} \) shows no reaction with sodium fusion followed by silver nitrate test. Which functional group is most likely present?

text_solutions: No reaction with Lassaigne’s test (sodium fusion + \( \ce{AgNO3} \)) indicates no halogens. \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \) (pentan-3-one) is a ketone, consistent with \( \ce{C5H10O} \), and lacks halogens.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method is used to estimate nitrogen in an organic compound by converting it to ammonium sulphate?

text_solutions: Kjeldahl’s method involves heating the compound with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) to form \( \ce{(NH4)2SO4} \), followed by ammonia liberation and titration.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which free radical formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) via homolytic cleavage is most stable?

text_solutions: Cleavage at \( \ce{CH2-CH2} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2.} \) (primary) or at \( \ce{CH2-CH} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH.CH2CH3} \) (secondary), which is more stable due to hyperconjugation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization state of the carbon atom in the carbonyl group of \( \ce{CH3CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The carbonyl carbon in \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) (acetaldehyde) is bonded to three atoms: one oxygen (double bond), one carbon, and one hydrogen. This involves \( sp^2 \) hybridization, forming a trigonal planar shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the presence of nitrogen gives a Prussian blue color due to the formation of which compound?

text_solutions: In Lassaigne’s test, nitrogen forms \( \ce{Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3} \) (ferric ferrocyanide) with \( \ce{Fe^{3+}} \), producing the Prussian blue color.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CH2C#N} \) attached to the ethyl group?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C#N} \), the carbon in \( \ce{CH2} \) has four single bonds (two H, one C to \( \ce{CH3} \), one C to \( \ce{C#N} \)), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is most likely to form during homolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) under UV light?

text_solutions: Homolytic cleavage under UV light splits \( \ce{C-Br} \) equally, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2.} \) (butyl radical) and \( \ce{Br.} \), typical in radical reactions.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which functional group is present in \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (propanoic acid) contains the \( \ce{-COOH} \) group, characteristic of carboxylic acids.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the total number of \( \pi \) bonds in \( \ce{CH3C#CCH3} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3C#CCH3} \) (but-2-yne), the triple bond (\( \ce{C#C} \)) consists of 2 \( \pi \) bonds.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: An organic compound with two \( \pi \) bonds has a total of 7 sigma bonds. What is its molecular formula?

text_solutions: Two \( \pi \) bonds suggest a diene or alkyne. \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH=CH2} \) (buta-1,3-diene) has 2 \( \pi \) bonds (two C=C) and 7 \( \sigma \) bonds (5 C-H, 2 C-C), fitting \( \ce{C4H6} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of isomerism is shown by \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) and \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) (propanal) and \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (acetone) have the same molecular formula (\( \ce{C3H6O} \)) but different functional groups (aldehyde vs. ketone), indicating functional isomerism.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method is used to estimate halogens in an organic compound by heating with fuming nitric acid?

text_solutions: The Carius method involves heating the compound with fuming \( \ce{HNO3} \) to convert halogens to silver halides.

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \) (but-1-ene) has one double bond (degree = 1). Its chain isomer, 2-methylpropene (\( \ce{CH3C(CH3)=CH2} \)), has a similar boiling point (~-6°C vs. -6.9°C), but cyclic isomers like cyclobutane (~12°C) can be separated by simple distillation due to a larger boiling point difference.

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C3H6O} \) is a functional isomer of propanal and contains a three-carbon chain with a carbonyl group. What is its IUPAC name?
